source_reports.citation: Waltemeyer, S.D., 2006, Analysis of the magnitude and frequency of peak discharges for the Navajo Nation in Arizona, Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2006-5306
source_reports.version: 1.0 (no revisions listed on the pubs page)

notes: Two reports. (1) Waltemeyer, SIR 2008-5119 (no revisions listed on the pubs page), the current statewide New Mexico report and NSS's citation 97 for New Mexico (NSS region 35): flood regions 1-9 at 7 recurrence intervals (2-500 years; no 200-year equation), equations and errors from Table 2 (pp. 9-10), limits from Table 1 (p. 8). In NSS these regions are gated by the parameter HIGHREG, which must equal the region's GC number (GC1092-GC1100 for regions 1-9); HIGHREG is a selector, not a regression variable, and is not stored. Equations are printed as K x 10^n A^a ...; intercept = log10(K x 10^n) (region 8's Q2 prints '8.990 x' with no power of ten; NSS uses 8.99). Variables, all log10: A = DRNAREA (mi2); S = BSLDEM30ff (the report labels average basin slope 'percent (ft/ft*100)', but its values, e.g. 0.0205-0.2023, and the worked example's 0.2422 are ft/ft, as NSS's BSLDEM30ff is); Pa = PRECIP (mean annual precipitation 1961-90, in.); E/1,000 = ELEV with scale 0.001 (the report divides elevation by 1,000); I24,100 = I24H100YA2 (NSS's code, whose name says NOAA Atlas 2, while Table 1 footnote 1 says the data are from NOAA Atlas 14, Bonnin and others, 2004). Error statistics: Table 2 prints log units directly; sep_log is the average standard error of prediction in log units and model_error_variance the square of the average standard error of regression in log units (the model error, p. 11). No covariance and no AVP are published, so intervals use sep_log. n_sites are the Appendix 1 gage counts per region (29, 62, 12, 29, 64, 23, 14, 28, 32; 293 in all, the report's total). Table 1 prints region 2's drainage-area maximum as '12,7000'; Appendix 1's largest region 2 gage is 12,700 mi2 and NSS uses 12,700, so 12,700 is stored. Other report inconsistencies (values stored as Table 1/Table 2 print them): Table 1's region 8 drainage-area maximum (1,200) exceeds every region 8 gage in Appendix 1 (largest 430), and Table 1's ranges for regions 6 and 8 equal SIR 2006-5306's Region 6 and High Elevation ranges; station number 09367680 is printed for two different gages (map 62, Chaco Wash, and map 65, Catron Wash); Appendix 1 gives 08478800's GIS drainage area as 1.80 mi2, but its predicted values and Appendix 2 use 0.20; a few Appendix 1 predicted values are misprinted (08390100 Q100 606,300 where the equation gives 60,600; 08480700 Q100 4,193 against 418; 07227100 Q2 330 against 3,020; 07153500 Q10 10,600 against 11,700). Apart from those, Appendix 1's predicted lines agree with Table 2: of 2,051 values, 2,034 are within 3% (median ratio by region and AEP 0.994-1.007). The p. 11 worked example (region 2 Q100, A 523, S 0.2422, E 6,940) prints 10,800 ft3/s; the equation gives 10,745 (0.5% lower), within the example's rounding of intermediate factors. (2) Waltemeyer, SIR 2006-5306 (Navajo Nation): regions 8, 11, High Elevation and 6, which NSS also lists for New Mexico (GC1088-GC1091), stored exactly as in CO.json and UT.json (region codes Navajo8, Navajo11, NavajoHighElev, Navajo6). Not stored: WSP 2433 (Thomas and others, 1997; NSS GC1079-GC1087), whose New Mexico regions SIR 2008-5119 updates. All values were double-entered (hand transcription from rendered pages vs. a programmatic parse of the PDF text) with zero disagreements, and every region and AEP equals live NSS at its 3 significant figures.
